sections.h2: Which Clay County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Clay County divides the work three ways. The Property Valuation Administrator decides what a parcel is worth, the Sheriff prints and collects the bills, and the County Clerk takes appeal papers and later inherits any bill the sheriff couldn't collect. Knowing which desk owns which question saves a seller several wrong-number calls.

All three share one building, 102 Richmond Road in Manchester. The PVA sets no tax rate and accepts no payments. Its work ends at the number on the roll.

Clay County property tax contacts
OfficeHandlesReach it

Clay County covers 471 square miles of Appalachian hills, with Manchester at the center. The 2020 count was 20,345 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 19,465 is 4.3 percent lower, so a listing draws from a shrinking local pool.

There are 7,288 households living in 8,781 housing units, and 76.4 percent of households own their home. A typical home is valued at $90,700. Typical rent is $724 a month, and typical monthly owner cost is $978 with a mortgage and $367 without. At those prices, any unpaid tax is a noticeable slice of the final settlement, so check the balance before you set an asking price.

sections.h2: How the PVA values a house
sections.html:
Value is pegged to January 1. Kentucky wants fair cash value, meaning the price a voluntary sale between informed parties would produce. Staff walk every parcel at least once in each four-year stretch, and new buildings join the roll every year.

A recent purchase can simplify things. If you bought in the previous year, the deed price may serve as next January's value, as long as nothing about the building changed. The state itself values only four categories: public service companies, bank shares, omitted tangible property and vehicles. Everything else, real and personal, belongs to the local PVA.

Beyond the annual value, the PVA's office follows ownership changes, maintains parcel maps, updates building details and administers exemptions on real estate. Before listing, ask the staff whether the map shows the right acreage, whether the building record lists a finished basement or an outbuilding that no longer stands, and whether the exemption on file still matches the owner.

Errors in those records flow straight into the bill. A garage that came down years ago but still sits on the record keeps lifting the value until someone asks for a correction. Visit during open hours, 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, or write to the office at 102 Richmond Road, Suite 200, Manchester, KY 40962.

The sheriff runs collection on Kentucky's fall-to-spring pattern. The Sheriff's page on the Fiscal Court website has a View Property Tax Bill button for parcel lookups. Call the sheriff's office at 606-598-3471 to confirm the exact opening date, since the state lets a county use 30-day phases when a different calendar is needed.

The usual state pattern looks like this:

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent off
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount
  • January: 5 percent added
  • February 1 to April 15: 21 percent added

Value is fixed on January 1, so a bill can carry the previous owner's name after a sale later in the year.

The steps come in a set order, and missing one closes the door.

  • Watch for the notice the PVA mails after raising a value.
  • Request a conference with the PVA or a deputy while the tax roll is open for inspection. That window starts the first Monday of May and covers two weeks, Monday through Saturday.
  • If talks fail, file the appeal paper with the County Clerk by close of business the next workday after the window ends.
  • Attend the local board hearing, held 25 to 35 days after inspection. The board gets five sitting days unless the state grants more.
  • Bring proof: sales of similar houses, an appraisal, or building costs. With no facts, the board has to deny you.

File and then fail to appear, and you forfeit the right to continue. An owner still unhappy afterward can carry the case to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Clay County gives it to people who live in the house and are at least 65 or classified as totally disabled. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the amount is $49,100, taken off the valuation before tax is figured.

Apply at the PVA office in Manchester, 606-598-3832. Age is shown with a driver's license, birth certificate or passport. A disability claim needs paperwork from the federal agency or retirement system that made the classification. Most disability claims renew annually. Exceptions cover owners with a service-connected disability and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid bill
sections.html:
When business closes on April 15, the sheriff hands the bill to the County Clerk. It becomes a certificate of delinquency and a lien on the parcel. Interest of 1 percent per month begins, and the clerk adds 10 percent while the county attorney adds 20 percent.

The county attorney writes to owners in May and, if necessary, June, and can arrange installments. From mid-July, certificates may be sold to outside buyers through late October. After a sale you owe the buyer, and more fees follow. The County Clerk's website posts a delinquent tax page for each year, which is the place to check whether a parcel was advertised for sale.

The Fiscal Court website, claycountyky.com, has a page for each department with contact details and hours, and the sheriff's page holds the bill lookup. The County Clerk's own site lists Recordings, Fees, Forms and an Open Records Request page.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill when you sell
sections.html:
The closing agent normally pays the current bill out of your proceeds and splits it with the buyer. An open delinquency has to be settled first, because the lien stays with the parcel. Get a payoff amount from the sheriff before signing a contract, and ask the PVA whether an exemption on the parcel ends when ownership changes.

The deed adds a separate charge. Kentucky taxes the seller $0.50 for every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts in full. The clerk takes it at the recording counter. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers, correction deeds and nominal gifts between parent and child fall outside the tax.

faqs.q: Who mails the Clay County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Sheriff does. If nothing arrives, call 606-598-3471 or use the bill lookup on the sheriff's page of the Fiscal Court site.

faqs.q: Can a Clay County owner contest a value in summer?
faqs.a: Generally no. Both the conference and the clerk filing must land in the May inspection window, with the filing due the next workday after it ends. Phone the PVA at 606-598-3832 in spring.

faqs.q: Does the Clay County PVA take tax payments?
faqs.a: No. That office only values property and processes exemptions. Money goes to the sheriff, then to the County Clerk after mid-April.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax owed on a Clay County sale?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The seller owes $0.50 per $500 of price, and the clerk collects it before recording. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers and correction deeds are exempt.

faqs.q: Can a Clay County house with a delinquent bill still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The delinquency gets paid at or before closing. Ask the County Clerk for the total with interest and fees so the title company can build it into the payoff.
